title: Identity, owner fields and authorization rules
description:
1. `Identity { sub, username, groups }`.
2. The contract's `authRules`: owner (default field `owner`, value `sub::username`, or `sub` as the contract says), `ownerDefinedIn(field).identityClaim(claim)`, `groups` with operations, `authenticated`, `publicApiKey`.
3. Owner fields are filled on create.
4. When `enforce_auth` is set, a violation gives `errorType: "Unauthorized"` and `data: null`.
5. Specs: user u2 can't update u1's Post; a group member can read; a catalog-style rule (members read, curators write).

Part of the `virtuus-amplify` crate (`rust/crates/virtuus-amplify`; workspace member; `@rust-only` specs in `features/amplify/`; cucumber runner in the crate; 100% coverage). Semantics: `~/Projects/Ripple/design/storage.md` **§2.2**, matching Amplify/AppSync behaviour exactly.
- **Contract format:** `~/Projects/Ripple/contract/contract.schema.json` (vendor a copy into the crate).
- **Fixture:** `features/amplify/fixtures/blog.contract.json`, hand-written in that format and shared by V8 and V9. It has `Blog`; `Post` with owner auth, an enum `status`, a customType `meta`, a hasMany `comments` and an index `postsByBlog` (partition `blogId`, sort `createdAt`); `Comment` with belongsTo `post`; and `Tag` with a composite identifier `["postId", "name"]`.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Decision (storage-lead, from the Apricitus web data-layer review): **the owner-field value is `<sub>::<username>`**, which is what AppSync writes for Gen2 userPool owner auth. `Identity { sub, username, groups }` fills owner fields with exactly `format!("{sub}::{username}")`. Owner checks match a record when its owner field equals that value (AppSync also accepts a bare `sub` for legacy data; accept both on read and write the `::` form). Clients query owner indexes (e.g. `cratesByOwner`) with that value. Add a scenario asserting the stored owner value after a create.
